<!-- pr-reviewer: c2399c0408c6f640b9a532dbeb627d4e0f08925c -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers. One follow-up issue is requested below (not blocking).

This review is at the safety-floor level (geometry import). The PR is a draft; this review does not flag it ready.

### What looks good
- The pin is a full rev on all six solidcore lines (`crates/kernel/Cargo.toml:30-40`). `Cargo.lock` changes only the six solidcore `source` lines and adds `serde` to the `solidcore-ops` dependency list. `serde` was already in the lock. There is no new package.
- The `build.rs` of `solidcore` is the same at `2016386` and at `fa67b3f`. The manifests of the six crates add only test targets and one description line.
- `step_diag::record_parses` (`crates/geometry/src/step_diag.rs:201-214`) changes only which diagnostic the user sees. The locator runs only after the parse of the whole file failed (`step_csys_read.rs:108-117`). A `None` from the locator shows the parser's own error. Thus a dense record can never make a bad file import. The new pin `a_dense_legal_record_is_not_named` also checks that a real fault after a dense record is still named.
- No assert was widened. Each moved pin is still an exact refusal or an exact closed form.

### Results (merged with main, locally)
The PR head already contains `origin/main` (`db3bb1f7f`); the trial merge was "Already up to date". All runs are local, debug, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`, `-j 6`.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-geometry`, full debug suite (39 binaries) | 308 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-kernel`, full debug suite (27 binaries) | 162 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored (`step_agreement` 29/29, `blend` 6/6, `machining_mesh_shortfalls` 3/3, `step_edge_gap` 6/6, `step_twisted_flank` 3/3) |
| `camcraft-app` targeted: `import`, the 13 `import_step_*`, `step_nesting`, `lead_approach`, `shoulder_adaptive`, `adaptive_fig8_crossing` (18 binaries) | 84 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored (`lead_approach` 7/7, `step_nesting` 9/9, `import` 26/26, `import_step_twisted_flank` 2/2) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Heavy lanes
`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches 106 steps, because `Cargo.lock` reaches every crate. By the owner's order of 2026-11-22, this review ran one targeted heavy step for the fig8 tests, in release:

- `app heavy: adaptive_fig8_crossing` (this review): ok, 2 passed (`adaptive2d_on_fig8_model_in_tight_stock_has_no_crossings_and_posts`, `adaptive2d_on_fig8_stock_excluding_top_face_has_no_crossings_and_posts`).
- `app heavy: known fail #2849 fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (this review): red as expected. It fails at `crates/app/tests/shoulder_adaptive.rs:330`, the line after the `// known-fail-assert` marker, with `EM-0800-4FL ends at selected face (dist 31.406, r 4)`. The marker stays valid.

The other reached heavy steps did not run here. They run at the cut. "Not run" is not a pass for them.

### The moved readings, checked
1. **`twisted_flank_off.step`.** The file is still refused, and the refusal names solid `#117`, the 0.343 mm gap and the 1e-3 mm limit. The user loses the face name. The location is still available: in `build_record` (`crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step/record.rs:158-169`) the candidate holds `body.worst_edge` (the kernel edge and the vertex point), but the refusal text drops it. `check_source_topology` (same file, lines 94-101) already turns the same value into "Input-record edge index N, vertex (x, y, z) mm". This is a lost diagnostic detail, not a wrong output. It does not block this PR.
2. **`edge_gap_021_stated_5mm.step`.** The new refusal is earlier and clearer: it names face `#46`, the 0.0210 mm gap, the 0.02 mm cap and the stated 5 mm. Note (wording before this PR, `crates/kernel/src/step_edge_gap.rs:73`): "the reader accepts twice that, from 0.01 mm to 0.02 mm" can read as "10 mm is accepted". "twice that, held between 0.01 mm and 0.02 mm" is more exact.
3. **Chamfer volume 802.667 -> 808 mm3.** I did the closed form again. Each corner of the 12 chamfer half-spaces is the octant region with `x+y<d`, `y+z<d`, `x+z<d`. The edge prisms give `6ad^2`. Each corner has three pair overlaps of `d^3/3` and one triple overlap of `d^3/4` (by symmetry: 3 x the integral of min(x, d-x)^2 = d^3/4). The removed volume is `6ad^2 - 8(3d^3/4) = 6ad^2 - 6d^3`. With a = 10 and d = 2: 1000 - 240 + 48 = 808. This is the exact volume of the intersection of the half-spaces, that is, three planes that meet in one vertex at (d/2, d/2, d/2). The old pin cut a further `d^3/12` tetrahedron at each corner (8 x 8/12 = 5.333). The new figure is the correct mitred corner.
4. **`MeshRefusal::Lenient`.** The arm is untested, not dead. `machining_mesh` calls `solidcore_tess::plan` first (`crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:300`), which is the display path. On that path `plan_or_fill` (solidcore-tess `mesher/mod.rs:1532-1546` at `fa67b3f`) still fills a refused face leniently and pushes it to `stats.lenient`. `judge` still refuses it (`machining_mesh.rs:160-165`). Only the provocation of case 3 moved to `NotWatertight { open: 6 }`, which is still a refusal. #3800 (P7) tracks a new provocation. That is sufficient.
5. **Toolpath pins.** `lead_approach` (7/7) and the fig8 heavy steps are green on this head.
6. **#2849.** See the heavy results above. #2849 is open.
7. **`Cargo.lock`.** Confirmed: only the six solidcore packages change, with no new package (see "What looks good").

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. Please file a follow-up issue (P7, `effort:medium`, `area:import`): "Name the edge and the vertex in the 'a vertex sits ... off its edges' refusal". The fix maps `body.worst_edge` to the input-record edge (and its face, if the record has the face) in `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step/record.rs:158-169`, as lines 94-101 already do. Then `import_step_twisted_flank.rs` can pin the face or edge again.
2. A dense record that also has a syntax fault is now not named by the locator, if the parser stops at its count limit first. The user then sees the parser's own error with its line number. This is acceptable, and it is not a silent acceptance.
3. The kernel heavy steps `machining_mesh_shortfalls` and `step_agreement` touch the moved readings directly. They run at the cut.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
